referents.why: 'say to him' (weqatal, third masc sg) follows 'go to Pharaoh'; the one addressed is Pharaoh
'my people' in the LORD's own words (cl3 'thus he says Yahweh'); the first person is the speaker, the LORD
referents.category: first person inside a quoted divine speech

referents.why: 'me' in cl5, inside the LORD's quoted words; the speaker is the LORD
referents.category: first person inside a quoted divine speech

referents.why: implied subject of the command 'go' (second masc sg), which the LORD gives to Moses in cl0
implied subject of 'you will say' (weqatal, second masc sg); Moses is told to say it
the imperative 'let go' sits inside the message Moses delivers to Pharaoh; its implied you is Pharaoh, the one addressed
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: third plural 'they may serve me' with the collective 'people' (w17), the people the LORD is releasing

links.why: self-link; a clause cannot be the next event after itself
the waw is fused into the weqatal, so 'and then': the second command follows the first
the waw joins a command to a change of person (third plural yiqtol), which the rules read as so that
'let go ... that they may serve me': a third-person yiqtol after a second-person command gives its aim
cl0 is the saying that introduces what the LORD said to Moses: the commands to go and speak
'you will say to him' introduces the message, whose saying clause is cl3
'thus he says Yahweh' introduces a collection of commands (let go; that they may serve me)

groups.why: the LORD speaks to Moses; the commanded speech to Pharaoh is a part of it, so the turn holds it as a part instead of cl1 and cl2 directly
Moses is commanded to say the message to Pharaoh; the commanded turn is spoken by Moses and holds the quoted LORD's words as its part (R2)
the innermost quoted turn: the LORD speaks to Pharaoh; the commands in cl4 and cl5 are its part; addressee added
'let go' is the command and 'that they may serve me' its aim; the builder used part, which is not a role of this kind
'Go' and 'tell' are commands joined by and at one level, so one imperative group with two command members. The builder's part role is not an imperative role.

none_fit.what: a command whose object is a speech; the imperative kind has no role for that, so it is recorded as the frame of the commanded turn
The imperative members (command, aim, basis, effect, warning) have no role for a speech that a command tells someone to make; the commanded speech is carried by a nested turn instead.
